title: 細胞生物学
subtitle: Cell Biology
educationalGoal: This course will help you understand: (1) the molecular mechanisms that govern basic cellular processes such as cell movement, proliferation and signal transduction. (2) the science behind what we know from modern biology. (3) the experimental techniques utilized to study cell biology in several model systems including yeast, frogs, fish, mice, and mammalian cells in culture.
advice: This course will help you understand some of the concepts by cultivating an understanding of the molecular mechanisms that govern basic cellular processes such as cell movement, proliferation and signal transduction. To cultivate your familiarity with the science behind what we know from modern biology, we will discuss the experimental techniques utilized to study cell biology in several model systems including yeast, frogs, fish, mice, and mammalian cells in culture. The lectures are designed to be interactive. In addition to instructor presentations, we will often break into short discussions about problems and analyze data. Additionally, students will give feedback in short questionnaires of the successes and failures of each lecture in order to continually improve the course. This course will work on your skills in scientific writing. We will discuss how to read and interpret primary contents in the textbook, and how to construct precise and concise scientific writing.
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of biochemistry, physics and chemistry. High school-level knowledge of biology.
